stages.note: Multicloud runs in a separate AWS account for the PoC. Pick the account first. Then, if you have no AWS identity yet that can create IAM roles and is not the root user, make one: path A (single sign-on, recommended for organizations with several people; it also turns on AWS Organizations) or path B (one IAM user with an access key, faster). Skip what you already have.

steps.h: Choose the AWS account for Multicloud
steps.d: Recommended: a new AWS account only for Multicloud. Multicloud's Terraform creates it in your AWS Organization in the stage “Connect AWS to Multicloud”; you need a sign-in to the management account of the organization (path A below turns on AWS Organizations) and an email address that no AWS account uses. A new account keeps the PoC apart from your other work, and you can close it later. Without AWS Organizations: create a new AWS account yourself at aws.amazon.com (it needs a payment card and its root login, so only you can do it), then use it as an account you have. An account that already holds other work: possible, but only after the warning in the stage “Connect AWS to Multicloud”.
in: Choice: new account (recommended), new account made by hand, or an account you have

steps.who: You, in the AWS console as root
steps.d: Sign in at console.aws.amazon.com as the root user. Open the account menu (your account name, top right) › Security credentials › Multi-factor authentication › Assign MFA device. Follow the steps for an authenticator app or a security key.

steps.h: Path A, step 1: turn on IAM Identity Center
steps.d: In the top search bar, type IAM Identity Center and open it. Select a region at the top right, for example us-east-1 or the region nearest to you. Click Enable, then Enable with AWS Organizations. AWS creates an organization for your account. Write down the region.

steps.h: Path A, step 2: create your user
steps.d: Open Users › Add user. Enter a user name, your email address and your name, then click Next twice and Add user. AWS sends an invitation email: accept it and set a password and MFA.

steps.h: Path A, step 3: give the user administrator rights
steps.d: Open Permission sets › Create permission set › Predefined permission set › AdministratorAccess › Next › Next › Create. Then open AWS accounts, select your account, click Assign users or groups, select your user, then the AdministratorAccess permission set, and Submit.

steps.h: Path A, step 4: copy the access portal URL
steps.d: Open Dashboard. In Settings summary, copy the AWS access portal URL (it looks like https://d-1234567890.awsapps.com/start). Sign out of the root user. From now on, sign in through this URL.

steps.h: Path B, step 1: create an IAM user
steps.d: Open IAM › Users › Create user. User name: poc-admin. Do not give console access. Next › Attach policies directly › select AdministratorAccess › Next › Create user.

steps.h: Path B, step 2: create an access key
steps.d: Open the user poc-admin › Security credentials › Create access key › Command Line Interface (CLI). Confirm the note and click Next › Create access key. Copy the Access key ID and the Secret access key: AWS shows the secret only once. Keep both secret, and delete the key after the PoC (same page › Actions › Deactivate, then Delete). Sign out of the root user.

stages.t: Sign in to AWS from the terminal

steps.h: Sign in to AWS from the terminal
steps.who: You, in a terminal and the browser
steps.d: Use the identity from the stage “Set up your AWS account”. Path A (single sign-on): run aws configure sso --use-device-code (on Windows the browser cannot open from WSL; the command prints a link and a code: open the link in your Windows browser, sign in, enter the code). Answers: SSO session name: any name. SSO start URL: your AWS access portal URL (in the AWS console, IAM Identity Center, dashboard). SSO region: the region where you turned on IAM Identity Center (the region selector at the top right of that console). Registration scopes: press Enter. Then select the account: for a new account that Multicloud's Terraform creates, the management account of your AWS Organization; otherwise the account you chose for the PoC (an account with other work only after the warning in the next stage) and the role AdministratorAccess (it must be able to create IAM roles; SystemAdministrator cannot, and the apply then fails with AccessDenied on iam:CreateRole). Never choose the root login. Default client region: us-east-1. Output format: json (press Enter). Profile name: poc. Path B (access key): run aws configure --profile poc and paste the access key ID and secret access key; region us-east-1; output json.

in.label: Path B: access key ID and secret

os.mac:
aws configure sso --use-device-code   # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity
os.linux:
aws configure sso --use-device-code   # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
aws configure sso --use-device-code   # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity

steps.g: The Account value in the output is your 12-digit AWS account ID. You need it in the next stage. Never paste keys into an AI chat. Path A: if your sign-in expires later, run aws sso login --profile poc. With --use-device-code the command prints a link and a code: open the link in any browser, sign in, enter the code. Later sign-ins: aws sso login --profile poc --use-device-code.
